title: Passing multiple tables to `with_for_update()` typing issue.
body:
### Ensure stubs packages are not installed

- [x] No sqlalchemy stub packages is installed (both `sqlalchemy-stubs` and `sqlalchemy2-stubs` are not compatible with v2)

### Verify if the api is typed

- [x] The api is not in a module listed in [#6810](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6810) so it should pass type checking

### Describe the typing issue

When passing multiple(here two) tables to the `of` argument of `.with_for_update(of=)` method, both Mypy and Pyright type checkers complains about the passed arguments.

Passing multiple tables is totally legal, for instance the [documentation of the postgresql](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE) says:

> If specific **tables** are named in a locking clause, then only rows coming from those tables are locked; ...


### To Reproduce

```python
Having the code:


from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column

class A(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "a"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)

class B(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "b"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)

stmt = select(A, B).with_for_update(of=(A, B))
```

Mypy raises:

```none
error: Argument "of" to "with_for_update" of "GenerativeSelect" has incompatible type "tuple[type[A], type[B]]"; expected "ColumnElement[Any] | _HasClauseElement[Any] | SQLCoreOperations[Any] | ExpressionElementRole[Any] | TypedColumnsClauseRole[Any] | <6 more items> | None"  [arg-type]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

and Pyright raises:

```none
error: Argument of type "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" cannot be assigned to parameter "of" of type "_ForUpdateOfArgument | None" in function "with_for_update"
    Type "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to type "_ForUpdateOfArgument | None"
      "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to "ColumnElement[Any]"
      "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is incompatible with protocol "_HasClauseElement[Any]"
        "__clause_element__" is not present
      "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to "SQLCoreOperations[Any]"
      "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to "ExpressionElementRole[Any]"
      "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to "TypedColumnsClauseRole[Any]"
      Type "tuple[type[A], type[B]]" is not assignable to type "() -> ColumnElement[Any]"
    ... (reportArgumentType)
1 error, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```


Also this issue only exists when we use `DeclarativeBase` new style. With previous style using `declarative_base()` there is no problem:

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = "b"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

stmt = select(A, B).with_for_update(of=(A, B))
```

### Versions

- OS: MacOS(Sequoia)
- Python: 3.12.6
- SQLAlchemy: 2.0.41
- Type checker (eg: mypy 0.991, pyright 1.1.290, etc):
mypy 1.16.1, pyright 1.1.402
